name: Predictable Id Collision
essence: Two same-tick customers receive the same receipt id and one stored receipt replaces the other.

examples.summary: Two same-tick customers receive the same receipt id and one stored receipt replaces the other.
examples.mechanism: A frozen shared millisecond clock supplies predictable identifiers; concurrent availability checks both pass before either insertion.
examples.expected_behavior: Two distinct receipt ids and receipts 2.

ingredients.suggests: The identifier uses only a shared millisecond timestamp.
Both callers check availability before either resumes to insert.

examples.summary: Two callers derive the same predictable identifier and separately check availability before inserting, overwriting one receipt..
examples.mechanism: Two callers derive the same predictable identifier and separately check availability before inserting, overwriting one receipt.

ingredients.suggests: The identifier contains only one shared millisecond reading.
Both callers check the same identifier before either resumes its insertion.

examples.summary: Two callers derive one identifier and overwrite one receipt despite individually protected map operations.
examples.mechanism: Two callers derive one identifier and overwrite one receipt despite individually protected map operations.

ingredients.suggests: Identifiers use a frozen millisecond stamp without a per-call component.
The availability check and insertion are separate critical sections.

examples.summary: Two callers overwrite one receipt key.
examples.mechanism: Both identifiers depend solely on the same millisecond timestamp. Callers release the map lock between checking the identifier and inserting it.
